title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill 2018
short_title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would incorporate tariff proposals removing duties on specified agricultural chemicals and clinical trial imports, and make a technical correction to Chinese tariff preferences.
The chemical changes would apply from 20 September 2017, while concessions for qualifying clinical trial kits and placebos would apply from 1 July 2018.
The chemical concessions would apply to all signatories of the regional free trade agreement covering Australia, New Zealand and participating Southeast Asian countries.
changes: Blinded clinical trial kits meeting by-law requirements could be imported without separately classifying their medicaments and placebos.
Placebos imported separately for use in Australian clinical trials would also receive duty-free treatment.
A redundant entry for herbicides and related products would be removed from the Chinese preferential tariff schedule without changing duty rates.
summary.affected: Importers of covered agricultural chemicals, blinded clinical trial kits and placebos for Australian clinical trials would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to introduce a free rate of duty for Indonesian insecticides and herbicides under the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, remove customs duty on clinical trial kits and placebos, and make a technical correction to the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement schedule.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill 2018, which removes customs duties on certain pesticides and herbicides from Indonesia and simplifies import rules for clinical trial materials, with a minimal financial impact of $3 million over forward estimates. The bill also implements Indonesia’s commitment to reduce tariffs on Australian sugar exports, benefiting Queensland sugarcane growers after Australian sugar exports to Indonesia fell from one million to 200,000 tonnes per year.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill 2018 introduces a free rate of duty for certain herbicides and pesticides from Indonesia under the Indonesia-Australia Closer Economic Partnership Agreement, creates a concessional item for eligible blinded clinical trial kits and placebos to remove customs duty and simplify imports, and removes a redundant item from schedule 12.
